subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — points on notice routing & evidence ownership
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form indemnity — quick internal alignment before I send redline

Team —

Acme returned a redline to the MSA/order form this morning. Their ask is focused on two things: (1) routing of notice and claim contacts (they want a single legal inbox on their side and a named contact on ours), and (2) allocation of responsibility for third-party IP claims when their customers assert infringement that traces back to model outputs.

I attached their redline (Acme_Redline_MSAv2.pdf) and a simple evidence matrix they included. My suggested approach:
- Accept a single notice inbox (procure@acmecorp.com) but keep our notice contact as an operations/legal alias (legal-claims@redwoodinference.com) rather than a named individual.
- For third-party IP claims tied to model outputs, propose the standard defend-or-reimburse split but add a short carveout requiring Acme to provide technical evidence (log snippets, prompt record) within 10 business days to avoid open-ended exposure.

Kimberly — can you draft language that: (a) makes our notice contact an alias; (b) requires a minimum evidence set and SLA for producing it; and (c) limits our obligation if the customer used the model in a way that violates our documented usage guidelines?

Ben — I expect procurement will loop in legal, but flagging that Acme is intentionally broad on the "AI-output" phrasing. We should be ready to trade a small liability cap for a clearer evidence & cooperation requirement if they push back.

I'll send a short note to Susan with our counter once we have the language.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

From: Susan Liang <susan.liang@acmecorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-09-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — Acme redline attached

Camila —

Thanks for the heads-up. We attached the marked-up MSA/order form (Acme_Redline_MSAv2.pdf) for your review. High level: Acme needs a clear path to route notices and a way to hold Redwood accountable where third-party IP claims are traceable to your model outputs.

Practical asks from our side:
1) A single mailbox for notices on our side (procure@acmecorp.com) to centralize intake across legal and procurement.
2) If Acme receives a third-party claim tied to outputs generated by Redwood, we expect Redwood to (i) take over defense when the alleged infringement is traced to model output originating from Redwood infrastructure, and (ii) indemnify for related damages.
3) We are open to a cooperation clause that requires us to provide logs/evidence, but we want the MSA to be explicit about acceptable evidence types and a 15-business-day window to provide it.

Two small asks: can Redwood confirm (A) who will be listed as Redwood's notice contact in the order form and (B) whether Redwood is willing to accept a modest cap (e.g., 2x fees in 12 months) in exchange for a clearer defend obligation?

I can loop in our outside counsel if we need pinning language.

Best,
Susan Liang
Sr. Counsel (Commercial) | AcmeCorp
susan.liang@acmecorp.com
Attachment: Acme_Redline_MSAv2.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-09-02T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form indemnity — draft counter language

Camila / Ben —

Draft proposed language below that reconciles Acme's requests with our production and risk posture. Please review; I kept the text concise so we can drop it into the redline.

1) Notices: "All notices under this Agreement shall be sent to legal-claims@redwoodinference.com and procure@acmecorp.com (or such other addresses as the parties may designate in writing). A notice sent to the designated address shall be deemed delivered on receipt."

2) Evidence & Cooperation: "Customer shall provide, within ten (10) business days of request, a reasonable set of technical artifacts to substantiate any third-party claim that Customer alleges arises from Provider's model outputs, which may include: (a) request/response timestamps; (b) redacted prompt and output text; (c) relevant model version identifier; and (d) any error/trace logs. Failure to provide the requested materials within the timeframe shall relieve Provider of obligations to indemnify to the extent such materials are necessary to investigate or defend the claim."

3) Defend vs. reimburse and cap trade: "Provider shall, at its option, (i) defend Customer against a third-party claim alleging that Provider's model outputs, when used in accordance with the documentation and usage guidelines provided to Customer, infringe a third party's intellectual property rights; or (ii) reimburse Customer for amounts finally awarded. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider's total liability arising from such indemnity shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid by Customer to Provider for the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (B) $200,000, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties."

Rationale: the 10-business-day evidence window is tighter than Acme's proposed 15 days to encourage quicker incident triage; the cap aligns to a middle ground while preserving defensive control (we keep the option to defend).

If you want to offer a concession to move negotiations forward, we can propose the cap as "2x fees or $200k, whichever is greater." Ben — think this would land okay with procurement?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

From: Susan Liang <susan.liang@acmecorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@acmecorp.com
Date: 2025-09-03T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — accepted language & next steps

Camila / Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Acme is comfortable with the notice alias and the proposed evidence list. Regarding the cap, Procurement is prepared to accept Provider's proposed cap so long as Acme retains the option to seek injunctive relief and additional remedies for willful misconduct.

Please proceed to upload the final redline to DocuSign (we will sign the MSA after Procurement issues the PO). We will also attach our evidence matrix (acme-evidence-matrix.xlsx) for clarity on the fields we expect.

Next actions:
- Kimberly: incorporate the three bullets into the redline and upload to DocuSign.
- Camila / Ben: coordinate with Procure to confirm PO timing; I'll follow up with procurement (procure@acmecorp.com).

Thanks — moving this over the line.

Best regards,
Susan Liang
Sr. Counsel (Commercial) | AcmeCorp
Attachment: acme-evidence-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
